tasks.short: Work with the crew at incidents, take part in crew briefings and debriefs, and pass shift information to the next crew.

steps.what: Firefighter collaborates with other firefighters as a member of a firefighting crew at incidents
Firefighter takes part in crew briefings and debriefs
Firefighter writes shift information for the next crew: on the station whiteboard today, on the station page after the change

tasks.design: Shift handover notes (vehicle status, open defects, agreements) go into a station page ({DOCS}) that the next crew reads on the station screen, instead of a whiteboard that is wiped. Working as a crew and debriefing stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handover lived on a whiteboard and in people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared station pages are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Crews change often and not everyone reads the page.
tasks.human_edge: Trusting a crewmate's call inside a burning building.

reach.learn: Whether open defects are known at the start of the shift.

evidence.claim: Shared station pages can replace whiteboards for shift handover.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident call to the shift handover; incident reports are outside.
Input contract: the station page is kept by the station; fallback is the whiteboard.
Crew work, debriefs and writing the handover (a first record) keep their full time. The page keeps information the board lost, but saves the firefighter no time.
The next crew reads the page in about the time it read the board.
research_questions: Are open defects known at the start of the shift more often?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: clearing finished items from the station page takes the place of wiping the whiteboard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high: writing the handover on a page takes as long as on the board, so no time is saved (0.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare training exercises, demonstrate techniques and coach new firefighters, assess their skills, and record training progress.

steps.what: Firefighter prepares training exercises for new employees
Firefighter trains new employees to control and suppress fires
Firefighter records training progress and skill sign-offs: in the paper training book today, on a tablet in the training system after the change

tasks.design: Exercises come from a shared exercise bank in the region's training system ({LMS}), so trainers adapt rather than write them. The firefighter enters progress and skill sign-offs on a tablet in the same system instead of a paper training book; this first record keeps its time. Demonstrating, coaching and judging skills stay with the firefighter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each trainer wrote own exercises and progress was kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Training systems hold exercise banks and skill records.
tasks.still_hard: Real fire behaviour cannot be fully shown in training.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a trainee's fear and helping them through it.

evidence.claim: Training systems can hold exercise banks and skill sign-offs entered on tablets.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training plan to the training record; certification exams are outside.
Input contract: exercise bank kept by the training department; fallback is own exercises and paper.
Coaching, assessing and recording progress (a first record) keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because exercises are adapted from the bank instead of written from scratch.
research_questions: Are skill records complete at the end of training?

incremental.description: Firefighter adds good exercises to the shared bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the bank has few exercises that fit the station, so most are still written (1.0); high: most exercises come from the bank (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take part in fire drills, give demonstrations of firefighting techniques to the public, and register drill attendance.

steps.what: Firefighter gives demonstrations of fire fighting techniques
Firefighter registers drill attendance: by signing a paper list today, by scanning the drill's code after the change

tasks.design: Drill attendance is registered by scanning a code in the training system ({LMS}), which counts toward each firefighter's competence record, instead of a paper list that the training office types in later. The scan takes the firefighter as long as a signature. Drills and demonstrations stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper attendance lists were typed into the training records.
tasks.enabler_now: Training systems register attendance by code scan.
tasks.human_edge: Showing children how to leave a smoky room calmly.

evidence.claim: Training systems can register attendance by scanning a code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the drill schedule to attendance registered; drill design is outside.
Input contract: drills planned in the training system; fallback is paper lists.
Drills, demonstrations and registering attendance keep their full time; the typing saved is the training office's, outside this role.
research_questions: Are competence records complete at the yearly check?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the firefighter: checking drill hours against the competence record stays with the training office.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high: a scan takes as long as a signature, so the firefighter saves no time (0.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the fire and situation on arrival and during the incident, and report conditions to superiors by two-way radio to receive instructions.

steps.what: Firefighter reports conditions to superiors using two-way radios

tasks.design: Nothing changes. Assessing a fire and reporting by radio happen in seconds on the scene; no software takes part.
tasks.previous_blocker: None; the task is on-scene judgement and radio talk.
tasks.still_hard: Smoke, noise and heat make the picture unclear.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a floor about to give way.

evidence.claim: Voice or location logs that show crew performance need works council consent, so radio traffic is not analysed per firefighter here.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident scene to instructions received; command decisions are outside.
Input contract: none; the firefighter is on the scene.
No new work: nothing changes in this task, so the added effort is zero.

incremental.description: No added work for the firefighter; nothing changes in this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high: the task stays fully with the firefighter.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The firefighter keeps fighting fires, training others and judging the scene; paper training books, attendance lists and whiteboards shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A firefighter with more time for drills.
